section: Supreme Court - composition, appointment, collegium and NJAC, jurisdictions (original, appellate, advisory, writ)
subsections: Transfer of judges and Memorandum of Procedure

accepted.s: Which one of the following recommendations was made by the Law Commission of India in its 14th Report (1958)?
o: Urgent review of the procedure for appointment of judges
Amendment of the Memorandum of Procedure to provide for women candidates
Creation of a National Judicial Appointments Commission
Direct appointment of members of the Bar to the Supreme Court without strict adherence to age or seniority
accepted.x: The 14th Report of the Law Commission, submitted in 1958, recommended that members of the Bar could be appointed directly to the Supreme Court without following age or seniority as rigid criteria.
accepted.tq: Match the recommendation with the correct institutional source and year.

accepted.s: The Law Commission's 214th Report, submitted in 2008, primarily dealt with which of the following?
o: Transfer of High Court judges under Article 222
Urgent review of the procedure for appointment of judges
Appointment of women judges to High Courts
Regional benches of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The 214th Report of the Law Commission of India called for an urgent review of the procedure for appointing judges.
accepted.tq: Use the year as the discriminator between closely related reform proposals.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Justice M. N. Venkatachaliah Commission:
1. It was set up in 2000 by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
2. Its report was submitted in 2002.
3. It recommended a National Judicial Commission for judicial appointments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution was headed by Justice M. N. Venkatachaliah, was established in 2000, submitted its report in 2002 and recommended a National Judicial Commission for appointments.
accepted.tq: Check the institutional sequence—setting up, reporting year and recommendation.

accepted.s: The Parliamentary Standing Committee in 2023 recommended amendment of the Memorandum of Procedure primarily to ensure that the Collegium recommends adequate representation of which of the following groups?
o: Members of Parliament and Governors
Women and marginalised candidates
Retired judges and legal academics
District magistrates and public prosecutors
accepted.x: The 2023 Parliamentary Standing Committee recommended amending the Memorandum of Procedure so that the Collegium recommends adequate numbers of women and marginalised candidates.
accepted.tq: Identify the target groups in a representation-oriented reform proposal.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the reform ideas associated with judicial appointments and accountability?
o: Abolition of the Collegium system by executive notification
A permanent disciplinary authority
Asset disclosure by judges
RTI coverage of the administrative side of the judiciary
accepted.x: The listed reform ideas include judicial standards and accountability legislation, a permanent disciplinary authority, asset disclosure, RTI on the administrative side and transparent appointments. Abolition of the Collegium system by executive notification is not included.
accepted.tq: Find the option that introduces a reform not contained in the stated set.

accepted.s: The expression “imperium in imperio” is used in the debate on the Collegium system to indicate criticism that it is
o: a forum exclusively for resolving Centre-State disputes
a self-contained authority operating within the State
a body subordinate to State legislatures
a constitutional body headed by the Union Law Minister
accepted.x: “Imperium in imperio” literally conveys the criticism that the Collegium functions like an authority within an authority, reflecting concerns about opacity and judges selecting judges.
accepted.tq: Translate the Latin expression into the institutional criticism it represents.

accepted.s: Which one of the following proposals was associated with the private member's Bill concerning judicial appointments?
o: Abolition of Article 222 and direct election of High Court judges
A 90-day limit for the Centre to notify Collegium recommendations, along with social diversity and regional Supreme Court benches
Appointment of all Supreme Court judges by State legislatures
Replacement of the Collegium by the Finance Commission
accepted.x: The private member's Bill proposed social diversity in appointments, a 90-day period for the Centre to notify Collegium names and regional benches of the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Separate the specific contents of a proposal from unrelated constitutional mechanisms.

accepted.s: Under Article 222 of the Constitution, a Judge of a High Court may be transferred by the President after consultation with the
o: Union Law Minister alone
Chief Justice of India
Chief Minister of the concerned State
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: Article 222 provides for transfer of a High Court judge by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
accepted.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” test to identify the constitutionally relevant authority.
accepted.sec: Transfer of judges and Memorandum of Procedure

accepted.s:
With reference to the appointment and transfer of High Court Chief Justices, consider the following statements:
1. Article 217(1) is relevant to their appointment.
2. Article 222 is relevant to their transfer.
3. The Chief Justice of India and two senior-most judges recommend candidates from outside their parent High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Appointment is linked with Article 217(1), transfer with Article 222, and the Memorandum of Procedure provides for recommendation by the CJI and two senior-most judges, generally from outside the candidate's parent High Court.
accepted.tq: Combine the relevant Articles with the institutional procedure rather than treating appointment and transfer as identical.
accepted.sec: Transfer of judges and Memorandum of Procedure

accepted.s:
Arrange the following steps relating to the appointment of High Court Chief Justices in the correct sequence:
A. Consultation with the concerned State
B. Recommendation by the CJI and two senior-most judges
C. Appointment by the President after consultation with the CJI and Governor
D. Consideration by the Union Law Minister
o: B, D, A, C
D, B, A, C
B, A, D, C
A, B, D, C
accepted.x: The sequence is recommendation by the CJI and two senior-most judges, consideration by the Union Law Minister, consultation with the concerned State, and appointment by the President after consultation with the CJI and Governor.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last steps, then place the ministerial and State consultations in between.
accepted.sec: Transfer of judges and Memorandum of Procedure

accepted.s: For appointment as Chief Justice of a High Court under the Memorandum of Procedure, the recommended judge is generally selected from
o: the State Public Service Commission
outside the judge's parent High Court
the same parent High Court only
the Supreme Court Registry exclusively
accepted.x: The Memorandum of Procedure provides that candidates for High Court Chief Justices should generally be recommended from outside their parent High Court.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to the intuitive but incorrect same-court assumption.
accepted.sec: Transfer of judges and Memorandum of Procedure

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional basis for establishing seats of the Supreme Court other than its principal seat?
o: Article 368 requires each regional bench to be approved by all State legislatures
Article 222 permits the Union Law Minister to establish regional benches
Article 130 permits other seats on the decision of the Chief Justice of India with the approval of the Centre
Article 217 authorises every State Governor to establish a Supreme Court seat
accepted.x: Article 130 permits the Supreme Court to sit at places other than its principal seat, subject to the decision of the Chief Justice of India with the approval of the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority and constitutional provision governing a proposed institutional change.

accepted.s: In August 2026, the Centre notified how many High Court judges?
accepted.x: The Centre notified 30 High Court judges in August 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the exact current-affairs figure and reject nearby judicial-strength numbers.

accepted.s: The first sitting of the Supreme Court of India took place on
o: 26 November 1949
15 August 1947
26 January 1950
28 January 1950
accepted.x: The first sitting of the Supreme Court of India was held on 28 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the first sitting from Constitution-related dates and Independence Day.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the strength of the Supreme Court is correct in relation to the stated 2026 development?
o: The strength was raised to 30 by a Parliamentary Standing Committee resolution.
The strength was raised to 50 by amendment of Article 130.
The strength was raised to 38 by an ordinance in May 2026 as the backlog approached six figures.
The strength was reduced to 38 by an order of the Collegium.
accepted.x: The sanctioned judge strength was raised to 38 through an ordinance in May 2026, when the case backlog was nearing six figures.
accepted.tq: Separate a numerical strength figure from nearby figures relating to High Court appointments and regional benches.

accepted.s: The High Court of Andhra Pradesh has been functioning at Amaravati since
o: 1 January 2019
1 June 2019
26 January 2019
1 January 2018
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court has sat at Amaravati since 1 January 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact commencement date from nearby constitutional and administrative dates.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

A. K. Subba Rao — Chief Justice of India from Andhra Pradesh
B. N. V. Ramana — Chief Justice of India from Andhra Pradesh
C. P. Wilson — Chief Justice of India from Andhra Pradesh
D. M. N. Venkatachaliah — Chief Justice of India from Andhra Pradesh
o: A and B only
B and C only
A and D only
C and D only
accepted.x: K. Subba Rao and N. V. Ramana are identified as Chief Justices of India who came from Andhra Pradesh. P. Wilson is associated with the private member's Bill on judicial diversity and regional benches, while M. N. Venkatachaliah headed the constitutional review commission.
accepted.tq: Start with the two sure regional associations and eliminate the reform-related distractors.

accepted.s: The principal reason for the Supreme Court's invalidation of the National Judicial Appointments Commission was that judicial independence is regarded as
o: part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution
a matter exclusively governed by ordinary legislation
a subject in the State List
a convention applicable only to High Courts
accepted.x: Judicial independence is treated as a component of the Basic Structure of the Constitution, which was the central constitutional significance in the NJAC decision.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional outcome to the constitutional doctrine that controls it.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding current debates on the Collegium system:
1. Its opacity has been criticised.
2. Executive delay in notifying recommended names has also been raised as a concern.
3. Calls for greater diversity and regional Supreme Court benches form part of the reform debate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The debate includes criticism of Collegium opacity, concerns regarding executive delays in notifying names, and demands for diversity and regional benches.
accepted.tq: Recognise that the debate contains criticisms of both judicial opacity and executive delay, not just one side.

accepted.s: The Punjab Cabinet's objection in September 2026 related to the allegation that
o: the Collegium had recommended only retired judges for Punjab
the Supreme Court had abolished the Punjab and Haryana High Court
the Union had transferred all Punjab judges to the Supreme Court
the State was bypassed in appointing the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court
accepted.x: The Punjab Cabinet objected that the State had been bypassed in the appointment of the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise administrative grievance rather than the broader issue of judicial appointments.

accepted.s: Which of the following developments was reported in relation to the Rajasthan High Court in September 2026?
o: The Chief Justice of India alleged nepotism by the Rajasthan High Court's Acting Chief Justice.
A Supreme Court judge alleged nepotism by the Rajasthan High Court's Acting Chief Justice.
The Rajasthan High Court was converted into a regional Supreme Court bench.
The Rajasthan Governor transferred the Acting Chief Justice without consultation.
accepted.x: A Supreme Court judge was reported to have alleged nepotism by the Acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court.
accepted.tq: Guard against the wrong-authority trap by identifying who made the allegation.

accepted.s: The Collegium named Chief Justices for which of the following groups of High Courts in August 2026?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, and Karnataka
Patna, Calcutta, Bombay, and Punjab and Haryana
Delhi, Madras, Kerala, and Gujarat
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Allahabad, and Chhattisgarh
accepted.x: The Collegium named Chief Justices for the Patna, Calcutta, Bombay, and Punjab and Haryana High Courts in August 2026.
accepted.tq: Use exact membership of the named group and reject substitutions from neighbouring High Courts.
